newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 2.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 2. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto said in his New Year speech that Indonesians should put national interest above all. He also said it was important for the Indonesiand to control their emotions in order to avoid the emergence of social conflicts.
At least five people were killed in capital Jakarta and in the nearby Bogor in a series of traffic accidents during the New Year celebrations.

Chairman of the General Elections, Yogie Suardi Memet, warned political parties against using government facilities in their election campaigns. Three political parties, the ruling Golkar, the United Development Party (PPP) and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are contesting the elections in May.
President Suharto said in his New Year speech that the national economy would face a number of challenges during 1997, such as the social gap and uncertainties in the global economy.

The Brokers' Club has protested against a plan by the Jakarta Stock Exchange to enact a new trading regulation which would prohibit employees of securities companies from buying and selling shares on the exchange.
